headlines: SPY 744.76 (-1.27%) at 17:06Z, back near the ~744 low after the late-morning bounce faded; Stocklake 16:09Z: SPY -1.16%, QQQ -1.71%, IWM -1.08%, VIX 21.62, Fear&Greed 35.5 (fear)

Fed Chair Warsh speaking at SF Fed/Fed Board Productivity and Jobs Task Force conference on economic impact of new technologies; quoted: 'the current era may be the most transformational period in my adult lifetime'
Axios: White House counsel requires agency sign-off before staff testify to Congress
Trending decliners: SMMT -15.3%, CAPR -13.9%, HELP -11.4%, IREN -9.1%, QBTS -7.0%, VKTX -6.4%; XPEV +6.2%; KO, HD flat
Econ: Canada CPI 3.1% y/y (core 2.0%), Japan Q3 GDP -0.1% annualised, China retail sales 0.4% y/y; US Retail Sales Tue 13:30Z (prev 0.8% m/m)

rumors.text: Warsh 'does not like AI' - his conference remarks read as negative for AI names
rumors.why: Would add policy overhang to the AI unwind; but his quoted line on a 'transformational' era cuts against this reading

rumors.text: Widespread AI capex cuts coming; 'AI bubble has burst'
rumors.why: Stale from earlier hours; if capex guidance really falls, semis and mega-cap tech drag the index

rumors.text: Neocloud/AI-infra names keep sliding (IREN -9%) as AI trade unwinds
rumors.why: Continuing theme; broad AI de-risking weighs on SPY's tech weight

rumors.text: Retail is over-levered buying the dip; a break lower would flush them (some now buying 740 puts)
rumors.why: Crowded dip-buying could amplify a break of ~744 support

plays.reason: Bounce off 744 faded after the Warsh appearance ('nothing burger'), QQQ leading lower, yet Stocktwits SPY (74) and NVDA (92) still bullish - no capitulation yet
plays.catalyst: AI/semis unwind; retest of ~744 low; Warsh remarks digested

readings.whats_new: The bounce to 746.5 faded and SPY is back at 744.76 (-1.27%), near the day's low; VIX rose to 21.6 and Fear&Greed slipped to ~36. Last hour's 'Fed chair speech at noon' rumor turned out true (Warsh at the SF Fed tech/productivity conference) but brought no rally; crowd sentiment remains stubbornly bullish, with NVDA still 'extremely bullish' on Stocktwits.
